item.description: Israeli President Isaac Herzog said he will announce on Sunday whom he will task with trying to form a new government, after the opposition's Gadi Eisenkot secured a commanding number of recommendations to replace Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

item.title: Africanews: Russia, Ukraine escalate mutual strikes in Black Sea ahead of Abu Dhabi talks
item.description: Russia’s defense ministry on Thursday claimed its forces struck a cargo ship carrying military supplies in the Black Sea just south of Odesa. This follows months of continuous attacks by Ukraine on vessels entering and leaving Russian ports in the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov.

item.title: BBC Africa: The new sports debuting at Africa's first Olympics
item.description: Chinese martial art wushu taolu has been among the eye-catching events debuting at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games.

item.title: BBC Africa: Why has Caf abandoned plans to hold Afcon every four years?
item.description: The Africa Cup of Nations will remain on a two-year cycle after the Confederation of African Football performed a U-turn on a decision taken last December.

item.title: Africanews: Tanzania opposition leader Tundu Lissu awaits verdict in treason trial
item.description: After 19 months in detention, Tanzania's main opposition leader Tundu Lissu will know his fate on Friday in a treason trial that has drawn international criticism and carries a potential death penalty.

item.title: Africanews: Transition to renewable energy key issue at COP 31 talks
item.description: UN climate negotiations beginning in Turkey next week will follow marked by a environmental disasters including heatwaves across Europe and catastrophic flooding in Nepal. A key issue at this year’s talks is the implementation of pledges to phase out fossil fuels.

item.title: BBC Africa: Tanzanian opposition leader found guilty of incitement
item.description: The 58-year-old, who has been detained since April last year, was acquitted of the more serious charge of treason.

item.title: Africanews: Kenyan cult leader faces death sentence over child murders
item.description: Last month, he was convicted of murdering 190 children and one adult between January 2021 and September 2023, alongside 28 co-accused. His lawyer said he would appeal.

item.title: BBC Africa: Kenyan court sentencing doomsday cult leader Paul Mackenzie
item.description: Paul Mackenzie was found guilty last month for murdering 191 people, all but one of them children.

item.title: BBC Africa: Somalia's top court rejects president's term extension amid political crisis
item.description: The country's first nationwide elections since 1969 are due next year - a timetable now thrown into doubt.

item.title: Africanews: Paraguay: Thousands protest banking scandal as president faces impeachment
item.description: Thousands of Paraguayans have taken to the streets over a banking scandal that has left nearly half the population without access to their savings. Protesters are demanding President Santiago Peña face impeachment despite his offer to resign.

item.title: BBC Africa: The young politicians with African roots making history in the US midterms
item.description: For some young Africans, these victories offer a glimpse of what a new generation of voters could do at home.

item.title: Africanews: Atiku’s candidacy in doubt after Nigerian court ruling
item.description: A Nigerian court Thursday declared invalid the nomination of Atiku Abubakar as the presidential candidate for the opposition African Democratic Congress (ADC), just two months before the country's elections.

item.title: Africanews: Refugee team competes at Senegal’s first Youth Olympics
item.description: Refugee athletes from camps in Kenya and Uganda are competing at the Youth Olympics in Senegal, marking the first time a refugee team has taken part in the event.

item.title: Africanews: West Bank: Palestinians harvest olives under Israeli military restrictions
item.description: Palestinian farmers in the occupied West Bank have been allowed limited access to their olive groves under Israeli military restrictions. Many found damaged trees, while soldiers fired tear gas near the harvest.

item.title: Africanews: Egypt army says hundreds of illegal gold miners arrested
item.description: At least 72 gold miners were killed, last October, by airstrikes on a gold mine on the Sudan-Egypt border. A rights organisation accused the Egyptian air force of carrying out the attack

item.title: BBC Africa: Will Atiku Abubakar be on Nigeria's presidential ballot after court ruling?
item.description: The high court has sacked the leadership of the opposition ADC party with only months to go until elections.

item.title: Africanews: Spain: Zelensky urges Latin America to help repair Ukraine's power grid
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has appealed to Spain and Latin American countries for urgent help repairing Ukraine's damaged energy infrastructure. He also met King Felipe VI during the Ibero-American Summit in Madrid.

item.title: Africanews: 'Fighting won't stop': Ethiopia clashes drive thousands into Kenya
item.description: Deadly clashes between armed forces in southern Ethiopia have driven tens of thousands into neighbouring Kenya with no idea when they can safely return home

item.title: BBC Africa: The new sports debuting at Africa's first Olympics
item.description: Chinese martial art wushu taolu has been among the eye-catching events debuting at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games.

item.title: BBC Africa: Owono left out of Eq Guinea squad after death of De Miguel
item.description: Goalkeeper Jesus Owono will miss Equatorial Guinea's Afcon 2027 qualifiers after asking to be left out of the squad following the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel.

item.title: Africanews: Moonshot 2026: Experts call for urgent reforms to unlock intra-African trade{Business Africa}
item.description: Experts at Moonshot 2026 in Lagos call for harmonised regulations and seamless digital payments to boost intra-African trade and as Silicon Valley pulls back, home-grown startups are stepping up to shape the continent's digital future.

item.title: Africanews: Guinea expels Burkinabé gold miners, draws Ougadougou's fury
item.description: More than 8,000 Burkinabé gold miners were forcibly expelled from Guinea-Conakry after authorities there imposed a ban on artisanal and illegal gold mining in several areas of the country's northeast

item.title: Africanews: Greece: Students march in Athens demanding more education funding
item.description: Thousands of pupils, students and teachers marched through central Athens on Thursday in a nationwide push for better-funded schools, joining a protest wave that has spread from France across southern Europe.

item.title: Africanews: Nigerian court nullifies Atiku Abubakar's presidential candidacy
item.description: A Nigerian court on Thursday declared invalid the nomination of Atiku Abubakar as the presidential candidate for the opposition African Democratic Congress, with just two months to go before the country's elections.

item.title: Africanews: Commonwealth leaders welcome UK dialogue on harms of transatlantic slave trade
item.description: Commonwealth leaders welcome Britain's agreement to engage in "time-bound inclusive and good-faith dialogue" over the "historical harms" of the transatlantic slave trade, during the closing press briefing of Commonwealth Heads of Government meeting (CHOGM).

item.title: Africanews: Cristiano Ronaldo announces international retirement from Portugal
item.description: Cristiano Ronaldo on Thursday announced his retirement from international football, ending a more than two-decade career with Portugal's national team.

item.title: Africanews: Experts gather in Namibia for nuclear test verification exercise
item.description: The Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty (CTBT) prohibits all nuclear weapons test explosions. Although it is yet to enter into force, a global norm against nuclear testing is emerging

item.title: Africanews: Extension of Mohamud's presidential term unlawful, Somalia's Supreme Court rules
item.description: Somalia's Supreme Court ruled on Thursday that the extension of the president's term by one year, which sparked violent clashes with the opposition, was “unlawful".

item.title: Africanews: A theatre festival in Morocco's capital celebrates six women directors
item.description: Six women theatre directors showcased their art and vision in the Jassad international festival in Rabat from October 27 to 30.
